examples.text: Потом был вкуснейший грибной суп, сваренный мною, затем куриные отбивные ..

glosses: A thin slice of meat, usually fried.
A chop, a specific piece of meat (especially pork, chicken, or beef) cut from the side of an animal.
A piece of fish that has been cut perpendicular to the spine, rather than parallel (as with a fillet); often synonymous with steak.
A prawn or shrimp with its head and outer shell removed, leaving only the flesh and tail.
A mash of vegetables (usually potatoes) fried with bread.
A cut of meat, often containing a section of a rib.

examples.text: Of the two fried chops served him for breakfast he ate one and gave Edmund the other, and put a buttered sandwich of bread in his pocket against the accidents of travel.
I only like lamb chops with mint jelly.
I was standing at the meat counter, waiting for some rib lamb chops to be cut.

glosses: A blow with an axe, cleaver, or similar implement.

examples.text: It should take just one good chop to fell the sapling.

glosses: A blow delivered with the hand rigid and outstretched.

examples.text: A karate chop.

glosses: Ocean waves, generally caused by wind, distinguished from swell by being smaller and not lasting as long.
A hand where two or more players have an equal-valued hand, resulting in the chips being shared equally between them.

examples.text: With both players having an ace-high straight, the pot was a chop.

glosses: Termination, especially from employment; the sack.
A woodchopping competition.

examples.text: E, C. McsEnulty, who won the chop at the show on Thursday, cut through a foot lying block in 34 seconds[.]

glosses: A crack or cleft; a chap.
Aircraft turbulence.
Cocaine.
A knife, especially one used as a weapon.

glosses: To cut into pieces with short, vigorous cutting motions.

examples.text: chop wood; chop an onion

glosses: To sever with an axe or similar implement.

examples.text: Chop off his head.

glosses: To separate or divide.

examples.text: We should chop off some of that department's budget.

glosses: to give a downward cutting blow or movement, typically with the side of the hand.
To hit the ball downward so that it takes a high bounce.
To divide the pot (or tournament prize) between two or more players.
To make a quick, heavy stroke or a series of strokes, with or as with an ax.
To do something suddenly with an unexpected motion; to catch or attempt to seize.

examples.text: Out of a Greediness to get both, he Chops at the Shadow, and Loses the Substance.

glosses: To interrupt; with in or out.

examples.text: This fellow […]interrupted the sermon, even suddenly chopping in.

glosses: To stab.

examples.text: A man had chopped a Sanitary Department coolie to death after an argument about money, Supreme Court was told today.

glosses: To remove the final character from (a text string).
To manipulate or separate out a line of cocaine.

examples.text: He chopped out a fat line.

examples.text: One of my bredrins is saying, what's the oldest ting he can chop?

glosses: To exchange, to barter; to swap.

glosses: To chap or crack.
To vary or shift suddenly.

examples.text: The wind chops about.

glosses: To twist words.

examples.text: Let not the counsel at the bar chop with the judge.

glosses: To converse, discuss, or speak with another.
A turn of fortune; change; a vicissitude.
A jaw of an animal.
A movable jaw or cheek, as of a vice.
The land at each side of the mouth of a river, harbour, or channel.
